citations.title: Personal Rights of Residents in all Facilities
citations.requirement: Lists 18 personal rights: dignity; freedom from punishment, humiliation, intimidation or abuse; being told how to complain to CCLD and the ombudsman; leaving at any time and not being locked in; private visits by ombudsmen and advocates at reasonable hours without prior notice; keeping and spending own money; phone, mail, voting and refusing care; moving out. Subsection (b) bars denial of admission, transfer, discharge, room sharing, room or restroom assignment, preferred name or pronouns, and association, based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status. Subsection (d): the Department cannot waive the (b) protections.

citations.title: Emergency Disaster Plan
citations.requirement: A written, readily available disaster and mass casualty plan. It must cover: administrative authority and staff assignments; fire safety plan; means of exiting; assembly at a predetermined evacuation site; transportation; relocation sites equipped for safe temporary accommodation; supervision during evacuation and contact after relocation; contact with fire, law enforcement and disaster agencies; and notifying a resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation. Emergency exit plans and telephone numbers must be posted.

citations.title: Personnel Requirements-General
citations.requirement: Personnel must be sufficient in numbers and competent. CDSS may require more staff when documentation shows a need. Anyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older. Staff assisting with personal ADLs get initial and annual training under HSC §§1569.625 and 1569.69, plus first aid from a qualified provider. Required training topics are listed, with trainer qualifications and documentation in personnel records. All personnel need a physician health screening (chest x-ray or intradermal test) within 6 months before or 7 days after employment. Criminal record clearance, exemption or transfer is required before employment or presence. Residents cannot substitute for required staff. Volunteers must be supervised and are not counted in the staffing plan.

citations.title: Incidental Medical and Dental Care Services
citations.requirement: Requires a plan for incidental medical and dental care. Staff may only assist with self-administered medications and may not give injections unless authorized by law. Assistance cannot include forcing, hiding or camouflaging medications. PRN rules: a signed, dated physician order on a prescription blank, with symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours. Central storage in a locked place, in the original container, with a record kept at least 1 year. Destruction by the administrator and one other non-resident adult, with a record kept at least 3 years. First aid kit; emergency numbers posted; ambulance number available; call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat to health.

citations.title: Admission Agreements
citations.requirement: Individual written agreement in 12-point type, plain language, with titled sections. Signed and dated within 7 days of admission. Copy given immediately, and a copy or notice of availability posted. Must specify basic services, additional services, rates, payment, 60 days' written notice of rate changes, refund conditions, preadmission fee limits and refunds, visiting policy, firearms policy, grievance procedure, eviction grounds and notice rights, and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman. LIC 9158 is required when the appraisal shows a hearing or other disability. No liability-waiver provisions.

citations.title: Prohibited Health Conditions
citations.requirement: Residents who need health services for, or have, these conditions cannot be admitted or retained: stage 3 and 4 pressure injuries, gastrostomy tubes, naso-gastric tubes, staph or other serious infection, total dependence on others for all ADLs, and tracheostomies. The list is not exhaustive ("including, but not limited to").

citations.title: Reporting Requirements
citations.requirement: (a)(1) Written report to the licensing agency and the person responsible for the resident within 7 days of any death, any serious injury as determined by the physician, any AED use, or any incident threatening welfare, safety or health (including unexplained absence or psychological abuse). (a)(2) Outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents: within 24 hours by phone or fax to the licensing agency and the local health officer. (a)(3) Fires and explosions: immediately to the local fire authority, and no later than the next working day to the licensing agency. (b),(c) Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult: report to the local ombudsman, licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours if serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours. (d),(e),(f) Written notice within 2 business days of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default notice or utility shut-off notice; notice to applicants before signing; civil penalty of $100 per day, up to $2,000. (g) Notice of a new administrator within 30 days. (h) Change of chief corporate officer within 15 working days.

citations.title: Night Supervision (RCFE)
citations.requirement: Fewer than 16 residents: a qualified person on call on the premises overnight. 16–100 residents: one employee awake on duty plus one on call within 10 minutes. Night staff must know the emergency plan and be first-aid trained. (Per fact-checked research S7.)

citations.title: Care of Persons with Dementia
citations.requirement: In homes with fewer than 16 beds, at least one night staff person must be awake and on duty when a resident with dementia needs awake night supervision, based on appraisal, reappraisal or observation. (Per fact-checked research S8.)

citations.title: Advertising Dementia Special Care
citations.requirement: A facility that advertises dementia care must have a written dementia program covering philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition and success indicators. Keep advertisements for 3 years. (Per fact-checked research S27 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Plan of Operation
citations.requirement: Written plan covering purposes and goals, admission agreement, admission policies, administrative organization, staffing and training plan, dimensioned sketches, transportation, handling of resident money, visiting policy, approach to resident behavioral expression, and the infection control plan. (Per fact-checked research S23.)

citations.title: Fire Clearance
citations.requirement: Fire clearance is required before licensure. A separate fire clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents. (Per fact-checked research S28.)

citations.title: Personal Accommodations and Services
citations.requirement: No more than 2 residents per bedroom; at least 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10, counting live-in staff and family. (Per fact-checked research S24.)

citations.title: Maintenance and Operation
citations.requirement: Heat of at least 68°F; hot water 105–120°F; plant maintenance standards; private water supply testing (annually for capacity 7–15). (Per fact-checked research S69 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Criminal Record Clearance
citations.requirement: DOJ and FBI fingerprint clearance or exemption is required for the applicant, administrator, adult household members and staff before they work or are present. (Per fact-checked research S29.)

citations.title: Safeguards for Resident Cash, Personal Property, and Valuables
citations.requirement: If the facility holds resident cash, it must keep receipts and accounting records and a separate account titled as the residents' money, with no commingling. LIC 400 affidavit and LIC 402 surety bond. (Per fact-checked research S70.)

citations.title: Administrator-Qualifications and Duties
citations.requirement: Administrator must be 21 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent and good character, and must be certified. Added education and experience for 16+ beds. Must be on premises a sufficient number of hours, with a designated qualified substitute when absent. (Per fact-checked research S14.)

citations.title: Infection Control Requirements
citations.requirement: Written infection control plan (LIC 9282). Name an Infection Control Lead trained by a qualified professional. Set initial and ongoing staff training. Review annually, after an outbreak declaration, or at the licensing agency's request. (Per fact-checked research S32.)

citations.title: Hospice Care Waiver
citations.requirement: Written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents; CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request. (Per fact-checked research S26.)

citations.title: Pre-Admission Appraisal
citations.requirement: Pre-admission interview and functional, mental and social evaluation, with consent and a suitability determination against admission criteria before admission. (Per fact-checked research S35 and the checklist.)

citations.title: Administrator certification
citations.requirement: 80-hour initial certification program (at least 60 hours live) and state exam within 60 days. 40 hours of CE every 2 years, including 8 hours on dementia. (Per fact-checked research S13.)

citations.title: Direct care staff training
citations.requirement: 40 hours initial: 20 before working alone and 20 within 4 weeks. The first 20 include 6 hours dementia and 4 hours postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice. 20 hours annually, including 8 hours dementia. (Per fact-checked research S10.)

citations.title: Dementia training for direct care staff
citations.requirement: Dementia training for direct care staff: 12 hours initial and 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S11.)

citations.title: Medication assistance training
citations.requirement: Homes of 15 or fewer: 10 hours initial (6 hands-on before assisting, 4 within 2 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. Homes of 16+: 24 hours initial (16 hands-on, 8 within 4 weeks) plus an exam; 8 hours annually. (Per fact-checked research S12.)

citations.title: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting
citations.requirement: Care custodians and facility staff are mandated reporters. Report by phone immediately or as soon as practicably possible, then in writing within the statutory time (SOC 341). The facility-specific 2-hour and 24-hour timeframes are restated in 22 CCR §87211(b),(c). (Per fact-checked research S36.)

citations.title: Liability insurance minimums
citations.requirement: Liability insurance of $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate for injury to residents and guests caused by negligence. (Per fact-checked research S18.)

citations.title: HCBS Settings Rule (applies to Assisted Living Waiver settings)
citations.requirement: HCBS settings must include a lease or agreement, privacy, resident choice, and access to food and visitors. Applies only if the RCFE enrolls in the Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver. (Per fact-checked research.)

citations.title: License fees
citations.requirement: Annual fee of $495.60 (4–6 beds) or $742.80 (7–15 beds), due each license anniversary, with a 50% late fee. Capacity change fee of $25. (Per fact-checked research S1.)

citations.title: Paid sick leave
citations.requirement: At least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year. (Per fact-checked research S57.)

citations.title: Meal and rest rules for 24-hour residential care of the elderly
citations.requirement: Special meal and rest period rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shifts need employment counsel. (Per fact-checked research S60.)

citations.cite: LIC 281 (Application Instructions for a Facility License), Sections A and B
citations.title: Application attachments (theft and loss policy B14; neighborhood complaint policy B15; sample menu B10; job descriptions B4–B5)
citations.requirement: Written theft and loss policy (B14); neighborhood complaint policy when the owner does not live in a home serving 6 or fewer (B15); sample menu (B10); job descriptions and personnel policies (B4–B5). (Per fact-checked research S21.)

citations.title: Workers' compensation coverage
citations.requirement: Workers' compensation insurance is required once the facility has employees; RCFEs are WCIRB class 9070(1). Cited in the fact-checked checklist; the section text was not fetched here and the URL is a code-index link only.

policies.title: Licensee Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The licensee's governing body is accountable under 22 CCR §87205 (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
The certified administrator must be on premises a sufficient number of hours, with a designated qualified substitute when absent (§87405). Designation is on LIC 308.
A new administrator must be reported to CDSS in writing within 30 days (§87211(g)): name, addresses, start date, background and qualifications, with certificate copy.
A change of chief corporate officer must be reported within 15 working days, with a fingerprint card (§87211(h)).
Residents and volunteers cannot be counted as staff (§87411(i),(j)).
Regulator: CDSS Community Care Licensing, Adult and Senior Care Program, (916) 657-2592.

policies.title: Administrator Certification, Continuing Education and Designated Substitute
state_specifics: Administrator must be 21 or older with a high school diploma or equivalent and good character.
80-hour initial certification program (at least 60 hours live) and state exam within 60 days of the course.
Fees: $140 application and $100 exam.
40 hours of CE every 2 years, with 8 hours on dementia, and no more than half self-paced.
Late renewal carries a $300 delinquency fee.
Administrator Certification Bureau: 916-653-9300, AdminCertInfo@dss.ca.gov.

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: Post the license.
Post or make available a complete copy of the approved admission agreement (§87507(e)(2)).
Post emergency exit plans and telephone numbers (§87212(c)).
Post emergency agency numbers, visible to staff and residents (§87465(f)(2)).
Post the ombudsman CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 and the local ombudsman number (research S58).
Annual license fee is $495.60 for 4–6 beds and $742.80 for 7–15, due each anniversary, with a 50% late penalty (HSC §1569.185).
Fire clearance is required, and a separate one before accepting nonambulatory or bedridden residents (§87202).
Change of licensed capacity fee is $25. Notify CDSS before changing capacity or location.
Advertising and license-number display rules are in §87206 (text not retrieved).

policies.title: Plan of Operation, Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: The plan of operation (§87208) must contain: purposes and goals; admission agreement; admission policies; administrative organization; staffing and training plan; dimensioned floor plan and grounds sketch (LIC 999); transportation; resident money; visiting policy; approach to behavioral expression; and infection control plan.
Job descriptions and personnel policies are LIC 281 attachments B4–B5.
Include an awake night shift duty statement.
Program flexibility requests fall under §87209 (text not retrieved).
Keep the manual on site; policies must be present for the pre-licensing inspection (research).

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Internal Compliance Review (facility-adopted; no state QAPI mandate verified)
state_specifics: No mandatory QAPI program for RCFEs was found in the verified sources. Keep this as an internal compliance policy.
Quarterly mock inspections (research checklist): medication records (§87465), personnel files for training, health screening and clearances (§87411), appraisals, and admission agreements (§87507).
Annual infection control plan review (§87470).
Track CDSS deficiencies and plans of correction.

policies.title: False Claims, Advertising Accuracy and Billing Integrity
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c) (only if enrolled in the Assisted Living Waiver)
state_specifics: §87207 False Claims and §87206 Advertisements (text not retrieved).
Dementia-care advertising requires the §87706 program; keep ads 3 years.
A separate charge is allowed only if listed in and authorized by the admission agreement (§87507(g)(3)(B)2).
Itemized monthly statement of charges (§87507(g)(3)(H)).
ALW residents pay their own room and board; waiver rates are billed only through DHCS-enrolled provider channels (research S68).

policies.title: Liability Insurance, Workers' Compensation and Bonding
state_specifics: Liability insurance of $1M per occurrence and $3M aggregate (HSC §1569.605).
Workers' compensation is required once the facility has employees (Labor Code §3700; WCIRB class 9070(1); research).
If resident cash is held, LIC 402 surety bond and LIC 400 affidavit are required (§87217; research). §87216 Bonding title confirmed only.

policies.title: Medi-Cal Assisted Living Waiver Participation and HCBS Settings Compliance (applies only if enrolled)
state_specifics: ALW operates only in 15 counties (Alameda, Contra Costa, Fresno, Kern, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, Sacramento, San Bernardino, San Diego, San Francisco, San Joaquin, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Sonoma).
Enrollment goes through DHCS: ProFacWAIVER@dhcs.ca.gov; WaiveProEnroll@dhcs.ca.gov.
The Medi-Cal enrollment packet includes a CY2026 application fee of $750 (research S65).
ALW providers need licensed nursing staff on call or employed. Facilities with more than 6 participants need an Individual Response System (research S47).
Tier rates run $95.69 (Tier 1) to $270.80 (Tier 5) per day. The waiver does not pay room and board. The SSI/SSP basic services rate is $1,444.07 a month (research).
HCBS settings elements: lease or agreement, privacy, choice, and access to food and visitors.
Federal EVV (42 USC 1396b(l)) is not shown to apply to RCFE residential services in the research.

policies.title: Resident Personal Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Implement all 18 rights in §87468.1(a) and post or distribute them as required. §87468 and §87468.2 (privately operated facilities) have titles confirmed only.
Residents may leave at any time and cannot be locked in. House rules such as locking doors at night or barring windows require Department permission (§87468.1(a)(6)).
Residents may keep and spend their own money, keep personal possessions, and have individual storage space, confidential phone calls and unopened mail.
Residents may receive or reject medical care and get help to vote.
Inform residents and representatives of the complaint procedure, including the CCLD complaint unit address and phone and the ombudsman.
Staff are trained on resident rights under §87411(c)(3)(C).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints (resident and neighborhood)
state_specifics: The admission agreement must announce the grievance procedure (§87507(g)(9)) and the right to contact CDSS and the ombudsman (§87507(g)(12)).
Procedures for residents to suggest policy changes must be specified (§87507(g)(8)(B)).
Residents must be told how to confidentially register complaints with CCLD, including the complaint receiving unit's address and phone (§87468.1(a)(4)).
Representatives' communications must be answered promptly (§87468.1(a)(9)).
Neighborhood complaint policy, LIC 281 attachment B15, is required when the owner does not live in a home serving 6 or fewer.
No retaliation against residents or staff who complain.

policies.title: Long-Term Care Ombudsman and Licensing Agency Access
federal: Older Americans Act (45 CFR 1324 Subpart A)
state_specifics: Ombudsmen and advocacy representatives may visit privately, during reasonable hours, without prior notice (§87468.1(a)(11)).
Post the CRISISline 1-800-231-4024 and the local ombudsman number.
Written notice to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman within 2 business days of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default or utility shut-off notices (§87211(d)).
Abuse reports go to the local ombudsman as well as licensing and law enforcement (§87211(b),(c)).
The admission agreement must state the Department's authority to examine resident records (§87507(g)(6)).

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Preadmission Fees, Rate Changes and Refunds
state_specifics: Agreement format: 12-point black type on plain white paper, one-sided, plain language, titled sections (§87507(a)(1)).
Signed and dated by resident or representative and the licensee within 7 days of admission. Give a copy immediately; keep the original and all modifications in the resident file.
Only one preadmission fee per admission. It must be refundable and described in writing. SSI/SSP recipients cannot be charged a preadmission fee or deposit. No damage deposits (§87507(g)(3)(C)).

Preadmission fee refund: 100% if the applicant decides not to enter before the preadmission appraisal, or if disclosure was not made. For fees above $500: at least 80% of the excess in month 1, 60% in month 2, 40% in month 3.
60 days' written notice of any rate or rate structure change, or as soon as notified of SSI/SSP changes. Rate change conditions are set under HSC §§1569.655 and 1569.657 as referenced in §87507.
Prepaid fees must be refunded as a proportional daily amount. If the resident gives 5 days' notice, refund at move-out. Otherwise refund within 7 days of vacating.
Refund of advance monthly fees on death follows HSC §1569.652 per §87507(g)(5)(A). Written notice goes to the payor if that is a different person.
Admission agreement must not contain liability waivers or prohibited provisions (§87507(h)).
LIC 9158 Telecommunications Device Notification for deaf, hearing-impaired or otherwise disabled residents (§87507(b)).
Blank agreement copies must be given to the public on request; copy fees at cost.

policies.title: Resident Funds, Personal Property, Valuables, and Theft and Loss
state_specifics: Decide at licensing whether the facility will hold resident cash. If yes: LIC 400 affidavit, LIC 402 surety bond, receipts and accounting records, and a separate account titled as the residents' money with no commingling (§87217; research).
Withholding a resident's money as punishment is prohibited (§87468.1(a)(3)).
Written theft and loss policy is LIC 281 attachment B14. §87218 (title confirmed) is the regulatory section for theft and loss.
Residents may keep and spend their own money and keep personal possessions (§87468.1(a)(12)).

policies.title: Advance Directives and Resuscitative Measures
federal: Patient Self-Determination Act principles (not applicable to RCFE as a provider type; do not cite 42 CFR 484)
state_specifics: §87469 governs advance directives and requests regarding resuscitative measures (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
Call 9-1-1 immediately for an imminent threat to health, except as §87469(c)(2),(3),(4) provides (§87465(g)).
Report AED use to licensing within 7 days (§87211(a)(1)(C)).
Residents have the right to receive or reject medical care (§87468.1(a)(16)).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
federal: 45 CFR 164.530 (only if the facility is a HIPAA covered entity, e.g., bills Medi-Cal electronically)
state_specifics: Confidential phone calls and unopened correspondence (§87468.1(a)(14),(15)).
Records access is limited. The Department may examine resident records (§87507(g)(6)).
Representatives are regularly informed of care activities as appropriate (§87468.1(a)(8)).
The facility must decide whether it is a HIPAA covered entity; the verified sources do not establish this.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination, SOGI/HIV Protections and Language Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d), if federal financial assistance is received
state_specifics: No admission denial, transfer, discharge or eviction based on actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status (§87468.1(b)(1)).

Room sharing, transgender room assignment by gender identity, restroom access, preferred name and pronouns, clothing and cosmetics, association, and consensual relations are protected (§87468.1(b)(2)–(8)).

A facility-wide restriction or ban on sexual relations is allowed only if applied uniformly and notified in writing to residents, representatives and prospective residents before signing (§87468.1(b)(7)(A)).
The Department cannot waive these protections (§87468.1(d)).
Use LIC 9158 for hearing disabilities. The admission agreement must be understandable (§87507(a)(1)(B)).

policies.title: Resident Council
state_specifics: §87221 Resident Councils (title confirmed; text not retrieved). Review the text before writing meeting frequency or staff-attendance rules.
The admission agreement must state how residents suggest policy changes (§87507(g)(8)(B)).

policies.title: Pre-Admission Appraisal, Suitability Evaluation and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Pre-admission appraisal covers interview, functional, mental and social evaluation, consent, and suitability against admission criteria before admission (§87457). Related: §87456 suitability and §87455 acceptance limits (titles confirmed).
Applicants may visit before residence with their representatives (§87468.1(a)(7)).
The appraisal triggers LIC 9158 if the person is deaf, hearing-impaired or disabled (§87507(b)).
Disclose any preadmission fee and refund terms before payment (§87507(g)(3)(C)).
Prospective residents must be told in writing, before signing, of foreclosure, bankruptcy, eviction or utility events (§87211(e)).
Admission policies are part of the plan of operation (§87208).

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
state_specifics: Required components, by section title: medical assessment (§87458), functional capabilities (§87459), mental condition (§87461), social factors (§87462) and reappraisals (§87463). Text not retrieved; confirm timelines before publishing.
Dementia night-supervision need is determined by appraisal, reappraisal or observation (§87705).
Staff must observe residents and recognize early signs of illness (§87411(d)(5); §87466 title).

policies.title: Individualized Service Plan
state_specifics: The admission agreement must explain how third-party services relate to the resident's service plan (§87507(g)(3)(B)6).
Basic services are listed in §87464 (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
§87467 requires resident participation in decisionmaking (title confirmed).
Representatives are regularly informed of ongoing evaluations (§87468.1(a)(8)).

policies.title: Retention Limits and Prohibited Health Conditions
state_specifics: Cannot admit or retain residents with: stage 3 or 4 pressure injuries; gastrostomy tubes; naso-gastric tubes; staph or other serious infection; total dependence on others for all ADLs; or tracheostomies (§87615(a)(1)–(6)).
The list is not exhaustive.
Exceptions and Department review are in §87616 and §87617 (titles confirmed).
Department health condition relocation orders are in §87637 (title confirmed).

policies.title: Allowable and Restricted Health Conditions, Bedridden and Nonambulatory Residents (CA-specific addition)
state_specifics: Allowable and restricted health conditions are in §§87609, 87611, 87612, 87613; these include home health agency use (§87609). Titles confirmed; text not retrieved.

Specific condition sections (titles confirmed): oxygen §87618, IPPB §87619, colostomy/ileostomy §87621, enemas/suppositories §87622, indwelling catheter §87623, managed incontinence §87625, contractures §87626, diabetes §87628, injections §87629, healing wounds §87631.
Care of bedridden residents: §87606. A separate fire clearance is required before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents (§87202).
Staff must receive 4 hours of training on postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice before working alone (HSC §1569.625).
Ambulatory-status limits: §87204.

policies.title: Eviction, Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Eviction grounds in the admission agreement must come only from state law or regulation, be worded exactly as shown there, and not be modified, except general house policies under §87224(a)(3) (§87507(g)(10); §87224).

The agreement must explain the resident's notice rights (HSC §§1569.682, 1569.683, as referenced in §87507), the process to file a complaint with the Department about the eviction, the relocation assistance offered, and the licensee's closure-plan responsibilities.
Cannot evict, transfer or discharge based on sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or HIV status (§87468.1(b)(1)).
If the Department orders relocation (§87223), the resident is not held to advance-notice terms. Refund what would have been owed had notice been given (§87507(g)(5)(B)).
Pay prepaid fee refunds on closure, sale or license forfeiture as specified (§87507(g)(5)(C),(D)). Preadmission fee refunds on forfeiture or closure must be paid within 15 days of issuing the notice.
Health condition relocation orders and the resident's right to request review: §§87637, 87638, 87639 (titles confirmed).

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Centrally store medications when refrigeration is needed and the resident has no private refrigerator, when the physician deems the medication hazardous in personal possession, or when it is a safety hazard to others (§87465(h)(1)).

Store centrally stored medications in a locked place accessible only to responsible employees, in the original container, with no transfers between containers. Only the dispensing pharmacist may alter a label (§87465(h)(2)–(5)).

Keep the record of centrally stored prescription medications for at least 1 year: resident, prescriber, drug, strength, quantity, fill date, Rx number and pharmacy, and custody instructions (§87465(h)(6)).

Destroy leftover prescription medications at the facility by the administrator and one other non-resident adult. Both sign a record kept at least 3 years listing resident, Rx number and pharmacy, drug, strength and quantity, and date. Hospice disposal procedures apply to hospice patients (§87465(i)).
Maintain a record of dosages of centrally stored medications when requested by the physician or Department (§87465(a)(6)).
Facilities of 16+ designate staff with primary responsibility for first aid and medication assistance (§87465(j)).

policies.title: Assistance with Self-Administered Medications and Staff Authorization (no administration by staff)
state_specifics: Staff may only assist with self-administered medications: those usually prescribed for self-administration and authorized by the physician, temporary minor illness, and tremor or failing eyesight (§87465(a)(5)). Staff may not give injections unless authorized by law.
Forbidden: forcing medications, hiding or camouflaging them without consent, or infringing the right to refuse (§87465(a)(5)(D)).

PRN medication: written physician order on a prescription blank, signed and dated, with symptoms, exact dose, minimum hours between doses and maximum doses per 24 hours; the label must match (§87465(e)).

If the resident cannot decide on PRN need but can communicate symptoms, the physician directions must include a discontinuation time or circumstance and when to recontact the physician. Record each dose with date, time, dose and response (§87465(c)).
If the resident can neither decide nor communicate symptoms, staff must call the physician before every dose and document the call (§87465(d)).

Staff training: homes of 15 or fewer need 10 hours initial (6 hands-on before assisting, 4 within 2 weeks) plus an exam, and 8 hours annually. Homes of 16+ need 24 hours initial (16 hands-on, 8 within 4 weeks) plus an exam, and 8 hours annually (HSC §1569.69).
Staff need knowledge to safely assist with self-administered medications (§87411(d)(4)).

policies.title: Incidental Medical and Dental Care and Emergency Response
state_specifics: Written plan for incidental medical and dental care: arrange or assist with care, and provide transportation, which may be limited to the nearest available facility that meets the need (§87465(a)).
Staff must know how to use residents' prosthetics, hearing aids and vision aids (§87465(a)(3)).
Complete first aid kit in a specific location, with a manual, sterile dressings, bandages, scissors, tweezers and thermometers (§87465(a)(8)).
Physician and dentist contact information readily available. Post emergency agency numbers. Ambulance service number readily available (§87465(f)).
Call 9-1-1 immediately for an imminent threat to health (§87465(g)).
Report AED use to licensing within 7 days (§87211(a)(1)(C)).

policies.title: Licensed Professionals, Home Health Agencies and Limits on Staff Nursing Tasks
state_specifics: RCFE staff are not licensed nursing staff. Services requiring specialized skills must be performed by personnel qualified by training or experience (§87411(h)).
Staff may not give injections unless authorized by law (§87465(a)(5)).
Use of home health agencies for allowable health conditions: §87609 (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
If enrolled in the ALW: licensed nursing staff on call or employed; LVN oversight (research S47).
Federal home health Conditions of Participation (42 CFR 484) do not apply to an RCFE.

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Observe residents and recognize early signs of illness (§87411(d)(5); §87466 title).
Call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat (§87465(g)).
Any serious injury (as determined by the attending physician) or incident threatening welfare, safety or health: written report within 7 days to licensing and the person responsible (§87211(a)(1)).
Reappraisal after a change (§87463, title confirmed).
Check §87615 prohibited conditions and §87637 relocation orders before readmission.
Document physician contact for PRN decisions (§87465(d)).

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
state_specifics: Homes under 16 beds must have at least one awake night staff person when a dementia resident needs awake supervision (§87705).

Dementia training for direct care staff: 12 hours initial and 8 hours annually (research; HSC §1569.626). The first 20 hours before working alone include 6 hours dementia; the second 20 within 4 weeks include 6 more.
If dementia care is advertised, maintain the §87706 program covering philosophy, admission, training, activities, environment, changes in condition and success indicators. Keep ads for 3 years.
Administrator CE includes 8 hours on dementia (HSC §1569.616).
Plan of operation includes the approach to resident behavioral expression (§87208).
Staff training includes recognizing signs of dementia (§87411(c)(3)(F)).

policies.title: Falls Prevention
state_specifics: A serious injury under facility supervision (as determined by the physician) requires a written report to licensing and the person responsible within 7 days (§87211(a)(1)(B)).
Call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat (§87465(g)).
Physical plant: non-slip surfaces, grab bars at toilets, tubs and showers, and emergency lighting (research checklist, §87303).
Observation of residents: §87466 (title confirmed).
Check resident reappraisal after falls (§87463).

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injuries
state_specifics: Stage 3 and 4 pressure injuries are prohibited conditions: no admission or retention (§87615(a)(1)).
Healing wounds: §87631 (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
Staff training on personal care, including bathing and toileting (§87411(c)(3)(B)).
Residents have the right to appropriate care that does not cause avoidable discomfort (§87468.1(b)(8)).

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
state_specifics: A hospice care waiver is required. Submit a written request stating the maximum number of hospice residents; CDSS decides within 30 days of an acceptable request (§87632).
Hospice care for terminally ill residents: §87633 (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
Notify the resident's hospice agency on evacuation or relocation (§87212(b)(3)).
Dispose of a hospice resident's medications per the hospice's procedures (§87465(i)).
Direct care staff need 4 hours of training on postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice (HSC §1569.625).

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Death of any resident from any cause, wherever it occurs (including a hospital, in transit or away from the facility), requires a written report to licensing and the person responsible within 7 days (§87211(a)(1)(A)). The report must include resident name, age, sex, date of admission; date and nature of event; attending physician's name, findings and treatment; and disposition.
Refund prepaid fees per the admission agreement and HSC §1569.652. Written notice to the payor if different from the responsible person (§87507(g)(5)(A)).
Destroy unreturned medications with the two-signature log kept for 3 years (§87465(i)).
Coordinate with the hospice agency if applicable.
Update the register of residents (§87508).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Use W&I §15630. Do not use the Lanterman Act.

Suspected physical abuse of an elder or dependent adult: report to the local ombudsman, licensing agency and local law enforcement within 2 hours if it results in serious bodily injury, otherwise within 24 hours (§87211(b),(c)). Written follow-up on SOC 341.
Psychological abuse by staff or residents, or any incident threatening welfare, safety or health: written report to licensing and the person responsible within 7 days (§87211(a)(1)(D)).
Residents have the right to be free from punishment, humiliation, intimidation and abuse (§87468.1(a)(3)).
Criminal record clearance before employment or presence (§87411(g); §87355).
Post the ombudsman CRISISline 1-800-231-4024.

policies.title: Incident, Accident and Unusual Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Written report within 7 days to licensing and the person responsible for: death, physician-determined serious injury, AED use, and any incident threatening welfare, safety or health (§87211(a)(1)).
Epidemic outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents: report within 24 hours by phone or fax to licensing and, when appropriate, the local health officer (§87211(a)(2)).
Fires and explosions: report immediately to the local fire authority and no later than the next working day to licensing (§87211(a)(3)).
Reports must include resident name, age, sex, admission date, date and nature of event, physician findings and treatment, and disposition.
Call 9-1-1 for an imminent threat (§87465(g)).
Keep incident reports with a copy of the notification to the responsible person.

policies.title: Elopement, Unexplained Absence and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Unexplained absence of any resident is a reportable incident: written report within 7 days to licensing and the person responsible (§87211(a)(1)(D)).
Call 9-1-1 if the absence creates an imminent threat to health (§87465(g)).
Residents may leave at any time and cannot be locked in. Door locking at night or window barring requires Department permission (§87468.1(a)(6)).
Awake night supervision for dementia residents who need it (§87705).
Search and notification procedures are facility-defined; no state-prescribed search steps were verified.

policies.title: Restraints, Postural Supports and Restrictive Practices
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c) (HCBS modifications must be documented, if ALW)
state_specifics: Residents have the right to be free from punishment and intimidation and from interference with eating, sleeping or elimination (§87468.1(a)(3)).
Residents cannot be locked into any room, building or premises (§87468.1(a)(6)).
Postural supports are governed by §87608 (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
Staff training on postural supports is 4 hours before working alone (HSC §1569.625).
Chemical restraint: staff may not hide or camouflage medications or force them (§87465(a)(5)(D)).

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan
state_specifics: Written disaster and mass casualty plan, readily available to the Department (§87212(a),(b)).

Required elements: administrative authority and staff assignments; fire safety plan; means of exiting; assembly at a predetermined evacuation site; transportation arrangements; relocation sites equipped for safe temporary accommodation; supervision during evacuation and contact after relocation; contact with fire, law enforcement, civil defense and disaster authorities; hospice notification (§87212(b)).
Post emergency exit plans and telephone numbers (§87212(c)).
LIC 610E is the application form for the plan.
Report catastrophes and major accidents within 24 hours (§87211(a)(2)).
Night staff must know the emergency plan (§87415).

policies.title: Fire Safety, Clearance, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Fire clearance from the local fire authority is required before licensure, and a separate clearance before accepting or keeping nonambulatory or bedridden residents (§87202). No fire-inspection fee for homes of 6 or fewer (HSC §1569.84).
Fire safety plan and means of exiting are part of the disaster plan (§87212(b)(2)).
Fires and explosions: report immediately to the local fire authority and by the next working day to licensing (§87211(a)(3)).
Fire safety rules are in §87203 and capacity and ambulatory limits in §87204 (titles confirmed). Drill frequency and equipment standards were not retrieved. Read §87203 before writing them.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control Plan
federal: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 (bloodborne pathogens; employees with occupational exposure)
state_specifics: Written infection control plan (LIC 9282) with an Infection Control Lead trained by a qualified professional (§87470).
Initial and ongoing staff training. Review annually, after an outbreak declaration, or at the licensing agency's request (§87470).
Staff training includes infection control (§87411(c)(3)(B)); the licensee must maintain infection control practices (§87465(a)(9)).
Serious infections such as staph are prohibited conditions (§87615(a)(4)).
Report outbreaks within 24 hours to licensing and the local health officer (§87211(a)(2)).
TB screening for staff: see STF-04.

policies.title: Smoking, Visitors, Pets and Firearms
state_specifics: The visiting policy follows HSC §1569.313 and must be in the admission agreement (§87507(g)(7)). Residents have the right to be told it (§87468.1(a)(10)).
Visitors, including ombudsmen and advocacy representatives, may visit privately during reasonable hours without prior notice if other residents' rights are not infringed (§87468.1(a)(11)).
Policy on firearms retained by residents must be in the admission agreement. If permitted, store per HSC §1569.282 (§87507(g)(8)(C)).
Facility house policies must be reasonable and not violate rights (§87507(g)(8)(A)).
No smoking or pet regulations were verified. Draft per local ordinance and the plan of operation.

policies.title: Food Service, Sample Menu and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Food Services regulations are in Article 10 of Chapter 8. No section number was retrieved; verify before citing.
A sample menu is required with the application (LIC 281 B10).
Staff need knowledge of good nutrition, food preparation and storage, and menu planning (§87411(d)(1)).
Plan of operation includes a food service description (research S23).
Under HCBS, residents must have access to food (if ALW).

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Planned activities: §87219 (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
Staff need knowledge of psychosocial needs such as recreation, companionship and independence (§87411(c)(3)(E)).
Residents may attend religious services of their choice voluntarily (§87468.1(a)(5)).
Dementia program (if advertised) must cover activities (§87706).

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry, Maintenance and Physical Plant
state_specifics: Resident rooms heated to 68°F minimum; hot water 105–120°F (§87303).
No more than 2 residents per bedroom; at least 1 toilet and washbasin per 6 persons and 1 tub or shower per 10 (§87307).
Private water supply testing: annually for capacity 7–15; for 6 or fewer only when evidence shows a need (research).
Residents are entitled to safe, healthful and comfortable accommodations (§87468.1(a)(2)) and individual storage space (§87468.1(a)(13)).
Staff need housekeeping and sanitation knowledge (§87411(d)(2)).

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: Transportation to medical or dental care may be limited to the nearest available facility that meets the need, provided directly or by arrangement (§87465(a)(2)).
Transportation arrangements are part of the plan of operation (§87208) and the evacuation plan (§87212(b)(2)(D)).
Any other facility transportation rules were not retrieved.

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Night Supervision and Supervision
state_specifics: No numeric day ratio. Staff must be sufficient in numbers and competent at all times. CDSS may require more staff based on documentation (§87411(a)).
Night supervision (10 p.m. to 6 a.m.): fewer than 16 residents need a qualified person on call on the premises. 16–100 residents need one awake employee plus one on call within 10 minutes (§87415).
In homes under 16 beds, at least one night staff person must be awake when a dementia resident needs it (§87705).
Night staff must know the emergency plan and be first-aid trained (§87415).
Everyone supervising staff or residents must be 18 or older (§87411(b)).
Residents cannot substitute for required staff. Volunteers are supervised and not counted (§87411(i),(j)).
LIC 500 Personnel Report shows coverage by shift. Include an awake night duty statement.

policies.title: Criminal Record Clearance and Background Checks
state_specifics: Before employment or initial presence, employees and volunteers subject to a criminal record review must obtain a California clearance or exemption, or request a transfer of a clearance or an exemption (§87411(g)).
DOJ and FBI Live Scan clearance is required for the applicant, administrator and adult household members before licensure, and for staff before they work or are present (§87355).
LIC 508 criminal record statement is part of the personnel documentation (research).
No RCFE-specific employee registry check was verified in the sources.

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Direct care staff: 40 hours initial. Twenty hours before working alone (including 6 hours dementia and 4 hours postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice) and 20 within 4 weeks (including 6 hours dementia). Then 20 hours annually (including 8 hours dementia and 4 hours postural supports, restricted conditions and hospice) (HSC §1569.625; §1569.626).
First aid training from a qualified provider such as the American Red Cross for staff providing care (§87411(c)(1)).
Required training topics: aging process; personal care and infection control; residents' rights; medication policies; psychosocial needs; signs of dementia (§87411(c)(3)).
Trainers must meet one of the qualifying criteria: degree plus 2 years' experience, health care license, or 2 years as an RCFE administrator within 8 years (§87411(c)(4)).
Documentation of training in personnel records. For on-the-job training, a trainer statement of content (§87411(c)(6)).
Medication assistance training per HSC §1569.69 (see HCS-02).
Facilities of 16+ meet §87411(d) with a planned on-the-job training program (§87411(e)).

policies.title: Employee Health Screening and TB Screening
state_specifics: All personnel, including the licensee and administrator, need a physician health screening with a chest x-ray or intradermal test not more than 6 months before or 7 days after employment or licensure (§87411(f)).
A signed physician report of each screening is required, stating whether the person is physically qualified and whether any condition creates a hazard.
Volunteers sign a statement of good health.
Staff with physical illness or emotional instability posing a significant threat to residents must be relieved of duty.
LIC 503 is the health screening form (research).

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Personnel records are governed by §87412 (title confirmed; text not retrieved).
Training documentation belongs in the personnel record (§87411(c)(6) cross-referencing §87412(c)(2)).
Include the health screening report (§87411(f)), criminal clearance documentation (§87411(g)) and training sign-in sheets.
LIC 501 Personnel Record, LIC 503 and LIC 508 are the application forms (research).

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff must treat residents with dignity (§87468.1(a)(1)).
No punitive actions, humiliation or intimidation. No withholding of money (§87468.1(a)(3)).
No discrimination on the bases listed in §87468.1(b); staff must use preferred names and pronouns.
Staff are trained on residents' rights (§87411(c)(3)(C)).
Residents may not be used as staff substitutes (§87411(i)).
No state-specific gift or boundary rule was verified; keep the facility's own standards.

policies.title: Wage-Hour, Paid Sick Leave and Meal/Rest Rules (CA-specific addition)
state_specifics: California minimum wage is $16.90 per hour from January 1, 2026. Local rates may be higher: City of Los Angeles $18.42 and San Francisco $19.61 from July 1, 2026; San Diego $17.75; San Jose $18.45.
Paid sick leave: at least 40 hours or 5 days per year (Labor Code §246).
IWC Wage Order 5 has special meal and rest rules for a sole caregiver in 24-hour residential care for the elderly. Live-in and 24-hour shifts need employment counsel.
SB 525 health care minimum wage applies only to RCFEs affiliated with or controlled by an acute-care hospital or its parent (research S61).
Exempt managers need at least $70,304 per year (research).

policies.title: Resident Records, Register of Residents and Retention
state_specifics: Resident record (§87506), documentation (§87505) and register of residents (§87508): titles confirmed; text not retrieved.
Keep the original signed admission agreement and all signed modifications in the resident's file (§87507(d)).
PRN physician orders and dose records stay in the resident's file (§87465(c)–(e)).
Centrally stored medication records are kept at least 1 year. Medication destruction records are kept at least 3 years (§87465(h)(6),(i)).
LIC 9158 is kept in the file when required (§87507(b)).
No other retention period was verified. Read §87506 before stating one.

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to the State
state_specifics: 7-day written reports: death, serious injury, AED use, threats to welfare, safety or health (§87211(a)(1)).
24-hour reports: outbreaks, poisonings, catastrophes and major accidents, by phone or fax to licensing and the local health officer (§87211(a)(2)).
Fires and explosions: immediately to the fire authority, by the next working day to licensing (§87211(a)(3)).
Abuse reports: 2 hours for serious bodily injury, 24 hours otherwise, to the ombudsman, licensing and law enforcement (§87211(b),(c)).

Notice within 2 business days to CDSS, the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, residents and representatives of foreclosure, unlawful detainer, bankruptcy, rent default or utility shut-off notice (§87211(d)). Notify applicants before signing the agreement (§87211(e)). Civil penalty of $100 per day, up to $2,000 (§87211(f)).
New administrator: 30 days. Chief corporate officer change: 15 working days (§87211(g),(h)).
Annual license fee due each anniversary (HSC §1569.185).
